title: Excellent WI-FI coverage; setup can be tricky; support may be questionable
text: For performance, I would rate this a solid 5-stars.  I bought a quality $300 router before this one and it just wouldn't fully cover the house with adequate wi-fi strength.  I spent $100 more on an extender, which finally helped somewhat, but still not ideal.  The router in this D-Link system has good strong wi-fi signal by itself, but it includes an extender which make it even better.  Excellent wi-fi coverage and also works good for wired connections as well.  For the price, the D-Link router is well worth the money.  So why not 5 stars in my rating?  The setup instructions turned out to be useless for me, but may have been because my internet was coming in through a router/modem combo; multiple routers on a network can cause issues and change how you might access a given router to set it up.  Support is important, especially when you are trying to set up for the first time, but I tried to call and there was a 25 minute wait, so decided to e-mail instead.  That was several days ago and the e-mail has not been answered yet, so I am disappointed in support, so that's one reason I knocked one star off my rating.  I strongly recommend you download the manual from their website, as the unit doesn't come with it.  The manual seems to be well written and comprehensive.  It still didn't help me with setup; I had to figure that out on my own.  If you have a straight-forward setup that is not complicated, you may not have any issues with setting up this unit.  Since this and most routers I have seen only have connections for 4 wired items, I am running an "extension" switch for more network devices and computer.  I could not get it to work at first, until a network expert told me that you have to reboot the router after you connect the switch, in order for it to be recognized.

title: Does Not Retain DPI Setting Reliably; Slightly Smaller Than Average
text:
I selected this mouse to be a spare for when I am on the go. Amazon-branded things are often of good quality so I was hopeful for this mouse. I came away a bit disappointed due to a couple of issues I have had with it.

This is a basic wireless mouse, suitable for surfing the web, working on documents or similar tasks. It’s not particularly good for gaming as it is not designed for such. If the goal is to have something that will allow you to casually use the computer for basic tasks, this one will serve. If you need a heavy-duty mouse for frequent use or you need a gaming mouse, spend a little more and get a more solid mouse.

One of the issues I have with mice is that I have huge hands and finding a mouse that fits my hand properly is a challenge. This is a smaller than average mouse, so it really doesn’t work for me. That’s not a big deal; it was designed for the large majority of people with smaller hands, so I can’t criticize this mouse for its size. It’s in that weird in-between size - smaller than the average desktop mouse but larger than a travel mouse.

The real issue I have seen with this mouse, though, is with the DPI setting. After idling for a little while, the mouse has a very nasty and predictable habit of resetting the DPI mode automatically. This is the only mouse I have used that has exhibited the problem. This impacts me when I am doing photo editing or using a graphics program and I need fine control. Sure, I can hit the DPI setting and get it to where I need it to be easily enough, but I should not have to do this over and over, particularly when I need the same setting all the time.

Other than the DPI setting, this mouse works exactly as expected. It is a decent mouse if you do not need predictable DPI settings. If you need a mouse that retains your settings, or if you need a larger mouse, or if you need a heavy-duty device, this is not the right choice for you. It’s fine for travel or casual use.

text:
For a long time I've had a little baby normal camera. Finally, I bought myself a digital camera to see what all the fuss was. And now I know.This is a great camera.

Pros:

> Amazing memory. I took over 400 pictures and still had room for more.

> Has an LCD screen, which really helps out night to see what you're taking pictures of.

> An incredible (almost overwhelming) selection of styles to take pictures. You have night pics, normal, manual, portait, camera...I could go on for ever.

> Disturbingly good zoom. You can zoom as far as to see the color of someone's eyes at at least 100yds. away. The zoom on this camera is scary good.

> For camera mode, the videos created are surprisingly clear with good sound. This is a great camera to double as a camcorder.

> Normally this camera takes excellent pictures, but, there are...

Cons:

> A wee bit bulky. Easy to hold in one's hand, but difficult to shove in a camera bag.

> The time lapse from the moment you press down on the picture button and the time the camera takes the shot is a little bit too long for my liking.

> Sometimes, the camera has a really difficult time to focus on stuff.

> While on camcorder mode, you cannot zoom in or out of a shot.

I'm being a little bit negative. I should stay on the positive. This is an amazing, stunning camera, worth every penny. I love it, and won't be buying a new digital anytime soon because I am really happy with this one. A must-have for any tourist on a trip or photography loving dork like me.

title: Impressive lens that is a bot difficult to focus well at first
text:
Toss out everything and start from scratch with this lens. First, on an Olympus OM-D EM-1 camera, the distance markings are worthless. Ignore them and use the screen to focus. Be absolutely certain to use electronic magnification while adjusting the focus, or you are going to miss more than hit. I find working in Manual Mode with Manual Focus is the best. An aperture around f/ 8 is my preference for bright subjects, but I have worked all the way down to wide open and gotten good shots. If you develop a mental checklist and go through it /every time/, you can get great results with this lens.

For my EM-1 and all other micro-4/3 cameras, the top and bottom of the circle are cut off some. I estimate that I still get over 80% of the circle area in my photo, and I am very happy with it.

Some subjects that seem to work well with this lens include landscapes, wind farms, museum falleries and cars.

Example photos are from The Early Ford V-8 Museum in Auburn, IN USA.

title: Disappointing. Difficult to record video 24/7. App stinks.
text:
I used a NestCam for about 4 years and found it to be phenomenal. My naughty parrot attacked the NestCam one too many times and finally did it in.

I decided to save $$ by purchasing this camer. It seemed like a fabulous deal at around $50 and the cost of a micro SD card (instead of paid cloud service).

IMO this camera is good for LIVE VIEWING and recording SPECIFIC scenes. However, it's not good for continuous 24/7 recording.

The PROS:
1) Nice-looking camera; looks like a robot :-)
2) Pan & Tilt capability
3) Easy to set up
4) Good price
5) Quality of video is decent
6) Responsive customer service
7) Good for "live" viewing

The CONS:
1) Horrible instructions
2) Difficult to set up continuous 24/7 recording (customer service helped me with this via e-mail)
3) Horrendous app aesthetically and performance-wise
4) Accessing recorded videos is tough since it records in "segments" of 2-15 minutes. You need to click on each segment individually to play that section of video. Does not have thumbnails for scrolling to activity on videos.

Perhaps I was spoiled by NestCam's app? This camera's hardware is good but the software and supporting documents need major improvement.

title: Loads of storage options; generally good build quality
text:
Bottom line: I’m pretty pleased with this laptop bag. There are ample (and I mean ample!) pockets and places to store items, but the design is such that it’s easy to keep things organized and get at what you need without a struggle. The internal padding does a great job of keeping laptops and tablets secure, and the build quality is mostly top-notch with just a few misses.

Full review: While I tend to dislike the term “tactical” when it comes to commonplace items such as bags, the design of this bag more than makes up for the choice of name. It’s styled in a way to mimic military gear, but it does so in a manner that doesn’t interfere with actual use.

The fabric is very thick and sturdy. This is a bag that can easily deal with getting bumped around without any risk of a fabric tear. The main zippers are also very nicely done. While the teeth are not metal, they are big and beefy, and have a smooth action. However, the smaller zippers, especially the one on an outside pocket, are not all that good. The teeth are small, and it can be a struggle to get them to open and close.

The top has a great feature: a lid that zips to keep it closed. As someone who has tilted my share of laptop bags and seen the contents hit the floor, the top lid is a wonderful feature. The top lid can also be closed with Velcro if you don’t want to deal with the zipper and/or want quicker access.

Lifting the lid leads to the main compartment, which is divided into two main areas by a full-length fixed divider. The divider and the outer walls are padded with a good amount of firm foam. One of the compartments has a half-height divider to hold things such as file folders separate from the laptop (or tablet). There’s a security strap that’s held in place by very sturdy Velcro to keep the laptop in place. The main compartment is about 14 inches wide and 12 inches deep (measurements were done by hand and are approximate).

The outside front of the case has four pockets. The two small ones have Velcro closures; the medium size one has a zipper; the large one has both Velcro and a quick-release buckle system. Aside from the poor zipper, all the pockets work well to hold a lot of items. The various sizes are handy to keep things organized.

The front also has a zipper so that it can be completely folded down, and allows access to slit pockets to hold papers and other thin materials.

The bag can be carried by an attached shoulder strap or a hand strap. I found both options to be very comfortable even when the bag was loaded down.

Misses are mostly minor. As noted previously, the pocket zipper is of so-so quality, and the pull tabs (which are strings) on all the zippers could be better in terms of comfort and utility. The bottom of the bag does not have any nubs or feet to keep it away from the ground when you set it down. Lastly, while it’s a plus to have buckles and straps for creating a custom fit, this has so many that they sometimes get in the way.

Those misses aside, this remains one of the better-built bags I’ve tried at this price point. While the misses brings my rating to 4.5 stars, I’ll round up to 5 since the looks, utility and comfort are outstanding for the price.
